note: Tecmo Super Bowl III: Final Edition (SNES) rates the 1995 NFL season. Every player of its 30 clubs but the punters as [name, franchise (scripts/data/nfl-teams.json), Tecmo slot, game position, overall, { rom: the game's spelling, no: jersey, attributes, id: nflverse gsis id }], written by scripts/sync-tecmo.mjs. The overall is ours, not the game's (conversion).

source.game: Tecmo Super Bowl III: Final Edition

dump.about: TSBTool2's data file of the stock SNES cartridge: 30 clubs of 37 players each, the free agents and an all-time team.

checks.name: NFTGL: The Book of Armaments, 2017 update

weights.about: The All Players sheet's point values (Man Pt Value) are the weights times its columns as it labels them, without the bonus terms (the club sheets add them). A few backs and receivers, most in one-back clubs' slots, are valued at another skill position than the one the sheet lists. Ours apply each weight to the attribute the screen names so.

names.about: A player takes nflverse's name when he is on his club's nflverse roster that season (or the one before or after) under the game's name: last names equal, cut short or a letter apart (two in a long name), first names equal, his given name, an initial, a short form or a letter or two apart, never both approximate. Else the game's spelling in ordinary capitals (gameSpelling). nflverse has no gsis id for some of the players it names.

source.leftOut: The cartridge's free agents (Deion Sanders among them) and its all-time team are no club of the season.

conversion.overall: Ours, not the game's: Tecmo rates no overall. Each player's NFTGL score at his game position is ranked among the season's players at that position (mid-rank percentile, ties sharing one) and read off Madden NFL 2002's overalls at that position (the 2001 season: maddenratings.net's 31 team spreadsheets, punters left out), as many of each Madden team's best as the season carries per club, by linear interpolation; rounded and held to 1–99.

formula.about: The NFTGL's weighting (The Book of Armaments, 2017 update; the league has revised its weighting over the years): per position, each attribute times its weight, summed, as the sheet's Man Pt Value. Its weights apply to the attributes the screen names so; the sheet's own sums give its RS weight to its first column, the screen's RP. Its bonus terms (50 or 100 points over thresholds of speed, rushing power, interceptions or hitting power) are no part of that value and are left out.

conversion.attributes: By the game's screen names, on its 16-step scale (6, 13 ... 100): RS running speed, RP rushing power, MS maximum speed, HP hitting power, BB body balance, AG agility, PS passing speed, PC pass control, PA passing accuracy, AR avoid rush (Tecmo Geek: avoid pass block), CO coolness, BC ball control, REC receptions, PI pass interceptions, QU quickness, KP kicking power, KA kicking ability, AKB avoid kick block. The dump lists RP before RS (TSBM 2000's order): they are swapped back.

positions.slots: QB QB; RB RB; WR WR; TE TE; C, LG, RG, LT, RT OL; RE, NT, LE (RE2, NT2, LE2) DL; ROLB, RILB, LILB, LOLB (LB5) LB; RCB, LCB CB; FS, SS S; K K; P left out. The nickel and dime slots: DB1 CB, DB2 CB, DB3 S, the position most of their players held (nflverse).
positions.skill: Backs, receivers and tight ends play their own position (nflverse's RB, FB, WR or TE) where nflverse names them, else their slot's: the game puts receivers in one-back clubs' back and tight-end slots and backs in their receiver slots.
positions.defence: Defenders play their slot's position, as the game has them (a tackle at inside linebacker is a linebacker).
